get.description: The Account Controls tab, soonest review date first. Optionally only one type (WALLET_FREEZE, FULL_FREEZE) and only those past their review date
The strongest active freeze, every freeze past and present, and every request raised against the customer. {id} is the customer's user id

post.description: Refused while anything in closure-check is in the way. On Compliance's approval the wallet balance at that moment is paid to the bank account shown, the account is closed and its sessions end; personal details are removed 30 days later. Needs a reason code, an explanation and evidence. Requires customer.status.propose

get.description: Lists what has to be settled first (live plans, loans, pending requests, a withdrawal in progress, a freeze on a wallet that still holds money), the wallet balance, and the bank account it would be paid into. bankAccountId picks one of the customer's saved accounts; without it their default is used

post.description: WALLET_FREEZE stops money leaving the wallet and new plan funding; money still comes in and loans can still be repaid. FULL_FREEZE makes the account read-only apart from loan repayments. Needs a reason code, an explanation, evidence and a review date at most a year away. Nothing changes until Compliance approves. Requires customer.status.propose

get.description: Active wallet and full freezes, freezes past their review date, and requests waiting on Compliance

post.description: Compliance sign-off: the change takes effect at once and is flagged on the audit trail. Re-checks the customer's freezes as they stand now. Refused for the administrator who raised it. Requires customer.status.approve
A note is required. Nothing changes for the customer and the proposer is told. Requires customer.status.approve

post.summary: Return an account-control request to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back undecided with a reason. Nothing changes for the customer and the proposer is told. Requires customer.status.approve; refused for the administrator who raised it
Only the administrator who raised it, and only before it has been decided
The freeze stays in place until Compliance approves. Any other freeze on the customer is unaffected. Requires customer.status.propose
Keeps the freeze in place past its review date. The new date must be later than the current one and at most a year away. Requires customer.status.propose

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the current user's investments, optionally filtered by product and by one or more statuses. Pass several statuses comma-separated (status=ACTIVE,MATURED) or repeated (status=ACTIVE&status=MATURED); paging and totals then cover only the matching investments
This endpoint retrieves total working capital and accrued interest across a customer's investments
This endpoint retrieves a single investment belonging to the current user

patch.description: This endpoint turns auto-rollover on or off for a plan that has yet to mature, and optionally changes whether principal only or principal and interest rolls. Switching on is refused where the product does not roll plans automatically at maturity; a MATURED plan is rolled over by instruction instead

post.description: This endpoint asks to break a live plan before maturity, with a reason, optional evidence and an optional waiver (hardship) claim. Only for products whose withdrawal rules route early exits through review (REAP always; RTN above its auto-release threshold) — a product that allows direct withdrawal is told to use the withdrawal endpoint, one that blocks early exit is refused with the rule named. The plan is held UNDER_REVIEW (no contributions, top-ups or adjustments; interest keeps accruing) until an administrator decides, or it matures. One pending request per plan
This endpoint cancels an investment that has not been funded

patch.description: This endpoint changes how often a goal is paid into and the day it lands, and reschedules the next debit onto the new day
This endpoint turns automatic contributions on or off for a goal, optionally switching the plan onto a card in the same call

post.description: This endpoint pays the amount a booking is waiting on, from the wallet or a debit card
This endpoint returns what the customer would receive if they withdrew now, with the penalty and tax breakdown. Nothing is persisted; echo the quoteHash on the withdrawal

get.description: This endpoint returns the interest payout cycles for an investment, including which one is awaiting a decision

post.description: This endpoint records whether a due interest cycle should be cashed out to the wallet or reinvested into the principal
This endpoint reinvests a matured investment into a fresh cycle, rolling principal only or principal and interest
This endpoint adds money to a live investment outside the contribution schedule. Where the product restarts tenure on top-up, the maturity date moves out

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the activity feed for an investment. Nightly interest bookings and the tax withheld on them are left out unless includeAccruals=true

post.description: This endpoint withdraws at maturity, liquidates early, or takes a partial withdrawal, settling to the wallet or a linked bank account
Accrues a day's interest. Pass a past date to backfill a missed run; days already accrued are skipped
Sends one 'added today' notice per daily goal for the given date. Goals already notified are skipped
Takes every wallet auto-debit due on or before the given date. Plans already advanced are skipped
Lapses unfunded bookings whose deadline is at or before the given moment (default: now), refunding anything that landed to the wallet
Tells customers whose wallet now covers a booking still awaiting funding. Debits nothing; the customer funds it themselves. Once per booking
Matures investments whose tenor has run on or before the given date
Settles interest cycles due on or before the given date, or parks them for a customer decision
Sends behind-schedule (60/30/15 days) and matures-in-30-days notices as of the given date. Reminders already sent are skipped

get.description: Every money-touching action waiting on a decision, from all six queues, newest first. Each item carries the target as it stood when the action was raised, the change asked for, and the target as it stands now, plus the fields that have moved between the two. An item whose target has changed in a way that matters is flagged stale with the reasons; staleness does not block approval, which re-checks on its own terms, it is so the approver is not surprised. canApprove is false with a blockedReason where the viewer raised it, does not hold the action's approve permission, or it has already been decided. Filter by status (PENDING, DECIDED, or a status name), module, action, proposedBy, or mine=true for the caller's own

Every entry written against plans and placements, in chronological order. All filters are optional and combine: investmentId for one target, actorId for every entry an actor took or approved, actorType (CUSTOMER, ADMIN, SYSTEM), module (investment, funding, contribution, accrual, payout, withdrawal, break, rollover, unlock), action for one event type, from/to for a window of days in WAT, flagged=true for break-glass and overrides, and propagated=true for entries a product-level change put onto a booked plan. order=desc reads newest first. Product configuration changes are a separate trail, read through the product configuration history

get.summary: Preview carrying the auto-rollover default across
get.description: Auto-rollover default is a forward-only (new-positions-only) field, so a change made in Product Management does not reach plans already booked. This answers how many booked plans would be switched on if it were carried across, and writes nothing

post.summary: Raise a propagation of the auto-rollover default
post.description: Asks for auto-rollover to be switched on for plans already booked against a product whose configured default is on. Nothing moves on submission: one of these can change every booked plan on a product, so it always waits for a second administrator. Refused where the product's default is not on, where a propagation for the same product is already queued, or where no booked plan would change. Only off-to-on is ever carried across: turning the default back off leaves booked plans alone, because a plan that asks to roll may be doing so on the customer's own instruction

get.description: Optionally filtered by status (PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED) or by product key

post.description: Second-admin approval: re-reads the product's configuration as it now stands, re-counts the booked plans and switches them on, writing the requester's reason to every plan's trail. Refused if the default has since been turned back off. The approver must not be the administrator who raised it
Declines with a note. Nothing has moved, so nothing is reversed and booked plans keep what they were booked on

post.summary: Return a auto-rollover propagation to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back to the administrator who raised it instead of deciding it, with a reason: the target has moved on, or it no longer makes sense as raised. Nothing changes on the target, the proposer is notified, and they raise a fresh one if it still stands. Needs the same permission as approving, and is refused (400) for the administrator who raised it.

The administrator who raised it takes it back before a second administrator has decided. Refused (403) for any other administrator, and (400) once it has been decided. Booked plans keep what they were booked on

get.description: This endpoint lists on-behalf investment requests, newest first, optionally filtered by status (PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED) and customer

post.summary: Create investment on behalf of a customer
post.description: This endpoint opens an investment for a customer on their written instruction. Written evidence and a reason are required. With second-admin approval disabled (the current setting) the investment is booked and, for a wallet source, funded in this call and the response comes back APPROVED with the booked investment; with it enabled the request is held in PENDING_APPROVAL for the approve/reject endpoints

get.description: This endpoint retrieves one on-behalf request with its evidence, reason and, once approved, the booked investment

post.description: This endpoint is the second-admin approval, used when approval is enabled (investment.on-behalf.approval-required). It books the investment for the customer and, where the source of funds is the wallet, debits the wallet in the same step; an external source leaves the investment awaiting funding. The approver must not be the administrator who raised the request
This endpoint declines a pending on-behalf request with a note. Nothing has been booked, so nothing is reversed

post.summary: Return a investment request to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back to the administrator who raised it instead of deciding it, with a reason: the target has moved on, or it no longer makes sense as raised. Nothing changes on the target, the proposer is notified, and they raise a fresh one if it still stands. Needs the same permission as approving, and is refused (400) for the administrator who raised it.

The administrator who raised it takes it back before a second administrator has decided. Refused (403) for any other administrator, and (400) once it has been decided. Nothing is booked for the customer

get.description: This endpoint lists every customer's investments, newest first. All filters are optional: product slug, status, owner (by id or exact email), a search on reference or name, a booking-date window, and flagged=true for positions marked prominent on the audit trail (break-glass, overrides)
This endpoint retrieves one investment regardless of owner, with the customer, contribution plan, payout schedule, event timeline, linked tranches and rollovers, and the full transaction ledger

post.description: This endpoint lifts an accrual suspension from the next nightly run. The suspended days are not back-filled

This endpoint pauses interest accrual on a plan from today, with a reason. The plan keeps its lifecycle state and can still be withdrawn; a withdrawal then pays interest as it stood on the suspension date

post.summary: Toggle auto-rollover on a customer's behalf
post.description: Switches auto-rollover on or off for a plan that has yet to mature, on the customer's written instruction (evidence and reason required), and optionally changes whether principal only or principal and interest rolls. A setting change, not a movement of money: it applies on submission with no second administrator, goes on the plan's trail with the evidence, and the customer is notified. Needs invmgmt.rollover.propose. Switching on is refused where the product does not roll plans automatically at maturity; a MATURED plan is rolled over through /rollovers instead. Asking for what the plan already has changes nothing and sends nothing

Takes a booking live on the amount that actually arrived rather than the amount it was booked for. The position is priced afresh for that amount, so a release into a lower band carries that band's rate. Only on products whose closed funding windows are resolved by an administrator (RTN by default); recorded on the audit trail with the reason

Writes the booking off: anything that landed against it goes back to the customer's wallet and the booking closes. Only on products whose closed funding windows are resolved by an administrator (RTN by default); recorded on the audit trail with the reason
Gives an unfunded booking more hours before it lapses. Only where the product's lifecycle allows an administrator to waive the window (RTN by default); recorded on the audit trail with the reason
Puts an UNLOCKED investment back to ACTIVE without withdrawing

post.summary: Roll over a matured investment on a customer's behalf
post.description: Raises a rollover of a MATURED investment on the customer's written instruction (evidence required), principal only or principal and interest, at today's rate. Refused with the plan's actual state where it is not MATURED, and where the product does not roll or the rate matrix cannot price the new size and tenor. Up to the product's on-behalf threshold (withdrawalAutoReleaseThreshold) it executes on submission; above it (or where no threshold is configured) it waits for a second administrator

post.summary: Top up on a customer's behalf
post.description: Adds money to a customer's live plan on their written instruction (evidence required), paid from the customer's wallet. Every rule the customer's own top-up obeys applies — the product must accept top-ups, the plan must be ACTIVE, the product cap and the customer's KYC tier ceiling both bind, and tranching or re-rating happens exactly as it would. Up to the configured admin-action threshold for TOPUP_ON_BEHALF it applies on submission; above it (or where no amount is configured) it waits for a second administrator

Last resort: moves an investment to the given state through the ADMIN_OVERRIDE trigger. Refused (409) unless the product's saved lifecycle lists an override edge for that move — the built-in defaults list none. Always flagged on the audit trail with the reason

get.description: This endpoint lists every move the product's lifecycle table allows from the investment's current state, with the trigger and actor each requires — what the detail page should offer as actions

post.description: This endpoint asks to unlock a customer's investment so an administrator can withdraw from it outside the product's rules. The investment is held UNDER_REVIEW until a different administrator approves or rejects. Refused (409) on products whose lifecycle does not permit unlock, such as RWIN

This endpoint raises a withdrawal on the customer's written instruction (evidence required). The product's withdrawal rules apply exactly as they do to the customer — a blocked or review-only exit is refused here with the rule named. Up to the product's withdrawalAutoReleaseThreshold it settles on submission; above it (or where no threshold is configured) it waits for a second administrator. An UNLOCKED plan is withdrawn through the unlock endpoint instead

Allowed only while the investment is UNLOCKED. Settles to the wallet or a linked bank account, optionally waiving the early-exit penalty; a full withdrawal closes the position, a partial one relocks it. Every step is flagged on the audit trail

get.description: Optionally filtered by status (PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED) or by investment

post.description: Second-admin approval: re-prices at today's rate, re-checks the plan is still MATURED and rolls it. The approver must not be the administrator who raised it
Declines with a note. The plan stays MATURED and payable

post.summary: Return a rollover request to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back to the administrator who raised it instead of deciding it, with a reason: the target has moved on, or it no longer makes sense as raised. Nothing changes on the target, the proposer is notified, and they raise a fresh one if it still stands. Needs the same permission as approving, and is refused (400) for the administrator who raised it.

The administrator who raised it takes it back before a second administrator has decided. Refused (403) for any other administrator, and (400) once it has been decided. The plan stays matured and payable

get.description: Requests to carry a statutory rate across to positions that are still running. Raised automatically whenever a tax rate is added or ended, because a plan is stamped with its rate at funding and would otherwise keep it for life. Optionally filtered by status (PENDING_APPROVAL, APPLIED, REJECTED)
One request, with the scope it covers, the rate before and after, how many running positions were in scope when it was raised, and whether it can be approved yet

post.description: Restamps every running position whose rate differs from the rate in force, and writes an audit entry per position keyed STATUTORY. Interest already booked keeps the tax it was withheld at. Refused if you raised it yourself, or before the rate has commenced
Leaves running positions on the rate they are stamped with, which will no longer be the rate in force. A note is required

post.summary: Return a statutory rate propagation to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back to the administrator who raised it instead of deciding it, with a reason: the target has moved on, or it no longer makes sense as raised. Nothing changes on the target, the proposer is notified, and they raise a fresh one if it still stands. Needs the same permission as approving, and is refused (400) for the administrator who raised it.

The administrator who raised it takes it back before anyone has decided. Refused (403) for any other administrator, and (400) once it has been decided. Running positions keep the rate they are stamped with

get.description: Alerts the engine raised for an administrator: a maturity run that could not roll or pay a plan, which stays MATURED until someone acts. Optionally filtered by status (OPEN, ACKNOWLEDGED, RESOLVED) or by investment

post.description: Marks the alert as seen by the signed-in administrator, with an optional note
Closes the alert once the plan has been dealt with (rolled over on behalf, paid out, or left to the customer), with an optional note

get.description: Optionally filtered by status: PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED, EXECUTED, RELOCKED

post.description: Second-admin approval: the investment becomes UNLOCKED and is flagged on the audit trail. The approver must not be the administrator who raised it
Declines with a note and releases the investment back to ACTIVE

post.summary: Return a unlock request to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back to the administrator who raised it instead of deciding it, with a reason: the target has moved on, or it no longer makes sense as raised. Nothing changes on the target, the proposer is notified, and they raise a fresh one if it still stands. Needs the same permission as approving, and is refused (400) for the administrator who raised it. The plan comes off its UNDER_REVIEW hold.

The administrator who raised it takes it back before a second administrator has decided, and the plan comes off its UNDER_REVIEW hold. Refused (403) for any other administrator, and (400) once it has been decided

get.description: Optionally filtered by status (PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED) or by investment

post.description: Second-admin approval: re-quotes at today's figures, re-checks the product's rules and settles. The approver must not be the administrator who raised it
Declines with a note. Nothing has moved, so nothing is reversed

post.summary: Return a withdrawal request to its proposer
post.description: Hands it back to the administrator who raised it instead of deciding it, with a reason: the target has moved on, or it no longer makes sense as raised. Nothing changes on the target, the proposer is notified, and they raise a fresh one if it still stands. Needs the same permission as approving, and is refused (400) for the administrator who raised it.

The administrator who raised it takes it back before a second administrator has decided. Refused (403) for any other administrator, and (400) once it has been decided. Nothing is moved on the customer's plan

This endpoint retrieves a single investment product and its published rates

patch.description: This endpoint updates an investment product's top-level fields. Retiring a product with live plans needs acknowledgeLivePlans=true (409 otherwise) and leaves it RETIRING until the last plan ends; setting a retiring or retired product back to ACTIVE undoes the retirement

post.description: Diffs a proposed product against the stored one and reports which field groups changed, their propagation categories, and the ceremony a save would run. Persists nothing

The live plans, customers and balance retiring this product would touch, and when its last plan matures. Persists nothing

The states this product uses, their labels, and every transition the engine will allow — as resolved for the product: the family's saved stateMachine configuration, or the built-in default when none has been saved (source says which)

What this product lets a customer withdraw before maturity and at what cost, as resolved from Product Management config, the lifecycle table and the product row: the early-exit route (DIRECT, REVIEW_REQUIRED, BLOCKED), holding period, review and auto-release thresholds, partial rules and the forfeiture schedule

Creates an administrator account holding the given TREASURY_PORTAL role and emails a temporary password. The temporary password expires (72 hours by default); login returns resetPassword=false until the admin sets their own

Administrators only. Separate from the shared POST /login, which is unchanged. The token holds only the account role; rights are read from the database on each request. Wrong credentials answer 401 with the failed-attempt count, as POST /login does. temporaryPassword=true means the admin must set their own password before going on

get.description: The signed-in admin's own record, with both role slots and their rights. Needs no directory right, so an admin holding only a portal role can load their own profile

post.description: The logged-in admin replaces their temporary (or current) password. Needs at least 8 characters with one special character. Sets resetPassword=true and clears the temporary password's expiry

put.description: Sets the administrator's role in the new portal, held alongside their legacy admin role so one account can use both. Pass a TREASURY_PORTAL role id, or null to remove the portal role. The legacy role is untouched

post.description: Issues a fresh temporary password, restarts its expiry and emails it again. Only for an admin who has not yet set their own password; the earlier temporary password stops working

Super administrator only. Emails the admin a temporary password (72 hours by default) that they must swap for their own on next sign-in; their current password stops working. Refused for a suspended/locked account and for your own
